name: Tikvah
overview: The name Tikvah appears in Scripture as a patriarchal figure connected to key individuals involved in significant religious events. Tikvah, also called Tikvath, is identified as the father of Shallum, whose wife Huldah the prophetess was consulted by royal officials during King Josiah's reforms, highlighting a family linked to prophetic ministry and spiritual leadership (2 Kings 22:14; 2 Chronicles 34:22). Additionally, Tikvah is noted as the father of Jahaziah, who, alongside others, was actively involved in matters of community restoration, demonstrating the family's ongoing role in God's covenantal work (Ezra 10:15). These references collectively underscore Tikvah’s place in the biblical narrative as a progenitor of those serving God's purposes in pivotal moments of Israel's history.
